issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong() (and instruct students to implement printFarmSong()), but the template and reference solution define and expect a method named singFarmSong() (and a private helper singFarmSongVerse). This name mismatch between the specification and the provided code can confuse students about which method to implement and may cause tests or grading to fail if they implement the method name indicated in the text rather than the template's method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either change the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() (and document singFarmSongVerse as the helper), or rename the public method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and adjust calls accordingly). Ensure the method name in the instructions, UML, template stubs, and solution match so students know which method to implement.
